newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dollar weaker in Europe, focus on French franc.
newsitem.headline: Dollar weaker in Europe, focus on French franc.

text.p: The dollar started trading on Monday off its overnight lows but still down from levels seen in Europe late on Friday, with attention in Europe focused on cross trading after the first round of the French election.
Dealers said the mark was stronger overall due to concern about the sharp swing to the left in the first round of the vote in France.

With most votes counted in metropolitan France, the Interior Ministry said the combined left had polled 40.1 percent, the RPR-UDF coalition and other right-wing candidates 36.5 percent and the National Front 15 percent.
Most of the 577 National Assembly seats were set to go to a run-off, where the behaviour of Front supporters and of the 31.6 percent of voters who abstained will be crucial.
The franc weakened by as much as five pfennigs on the news, but stabilised to around 29.62 marks per 100 francs in morning trade.
Dealers warned, howevver, that there could be a larger sell-off if next week's poll confirmed the trend to the left.
"If this trend is confirmed next week then it would signal the euro is in danger," one trader at a German bank said, adding that the natural response would be a firmer mark.
Trade on the dollar was quiet, with volumes thinned by holidays today in Britain and the United States.
"It is likely to remain quiet today," one trader said.
The dollar was trading at 1.6853/63 marks at 0825 GMT after bouncing off overnight lows of 1.6770/80 marks.
